posts.cooked:
OK, part 1 of this write-up (not sure how much I'll finish tonight before going to bed):

My lineup consisted of Legacy, Nightmist, Absolute Zero, Unity, and Tempest, in that order for all of the games. I decided in advance to work from easiest villain to hardest, and to run all of them in Advanced mode. Since I don't own Shattered Timelines, I used Ambuscade as a "nemesis" for Absolute Zero and Cosmic Omnitron as the "nemesis" for Unity.

The first match against Baron Blade took place in Insula Primalis. After the Baron put out a Living Force Field on his first turn, things got dicey for just a few rounds. So dicey, in fact, that we flipped the Baron on the last possible turn (his post-turn discard put 17 cards into his trash) since we lost some equipment and ongoings to the Baron over the first few rounds and had dinosaurs to deal with on top of the rest. Once we flipped him, we managed to get a sequence of cards that let us pummel the Baron at will.

 

Round 2, against Ambuscade -- I can't remember where right now, but think it might have been Atlantis -- started with him staying under the cloak for a round while we pummeled it and both Reactive Platings. Even on Advanced Mode, he didn't have much way to stop us building up and we just steamrolled him.

Round 3 was against Gloomy in the Realm of Discord (only fitting). We managed to keep the Zombies and Cultists under control, and hit the Grimoire early. However, it made the most sense to focus on pummeling Gloomy himself since we had lost of energy tupes available, and it only got dicey at the end when Time Flies triggered two consecutive Vast Followings. However, at that point Gloomweaver had been flipped and under 20 hit points, so we managed to survive the end of his turn and finish kicking the crap out of him.

I'll try to write up the rest tomorrow, but the short version is that Voss was a tough fight but doable, while Cosmitron very nearly cleaned our clocks -- Frost was into "survive" mode and it was the Police Backup that fired off the winning shot.
